transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Reddy (Redwood SE), Sofia Martinez (Redwood Product), Dana Park (Fluxlytics CTO), Liam O'Neal (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Security), Oliver Grant (Product)

Summary: quick migration/parity demo to show how Fluxlytics can map current OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls to Redwood API, discuss latency/cost tradeoffs, security (KMS/SSO/SOC2), and plan a benchmark.

00:00:02 Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll do a 30–45 minute walkthrough, demo the API, the Console, and the Optimize suggestions, and then leave time for Q&A. Dana, thanks for getting the team together.
00:00:12 Dana (CTO): yeah, thanks. trying to move off a mix of OpenAI and Anthropic calls, some evals on Together models too, so curious on parity and costs.
00:00:25 Arjun (SE): awesome — quick agenda: mapping of parameters (temperature, max_tokens, stop sequences, streaming), model parity and variants, Console walkthrough (rollouts, metrics), Optimize recommendations (batching, quantization), and then security notes.
00:00:40 Liam (ML Eng): two things up front — we care about latency p95 under 350ms for short prompts, and we use function calling heavily and streaming tokens to clients. How smooth is that?
00:00:55 Arjun (SE): great — Redwood supports streaming and function/tool calling. The mapping is mostly 1:1 — e.g., OpenAI "max_tokens" maps to Redwood's "max_tokens", Anthropic's "max_tokens_to_sample" maps too but we call out different name in examples. We'll show code snippets.
00:01:12 Priya (Security): and SOC 2 / KMS, we need audit logs and customer-managed key options — is that covered?
00:01:20 Sofia (Product): yes, we have private deployments and KMS/HSM options, audit logs, and RBAC. We'll drop the security pack after the call.

01:02:05 Maya (AE): okay starting the demo — Console home, project view, model catalog — you can see we surface latency/cost per route. For parity mapping there are in-console quickstarts: OpenAI -> Redwood header change, Anthropic -> Redwood mapping, Together -> Redwood mapping.
01:02:28 Arjun (SE): here's a code snippet — OpenAI curl: 
curl https://api.openai.com/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENAI_KEY" -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","prompt":"...","temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":150}'

01:02:48 Arjun (SE): Redwood equivalent is: 
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood-mix-1","prompt":"...","temperature":0.2,"max_tokens":150}'

01:03:05 Liam: ok so looks like mostly endpoint and model name change, any tokenization diffs? we have some prompt-length assumptions.
01:03:15 Arjun: good q — in most cases subtoken counts are within margin but yes some models tokenize differently; we recommend running your tokenization check and we provide a small tokenizer tool in Console to compare OpenAI/GPT/Anthropic/Together token counts against Redwood models. we'll include that in the parity doc.
01:03:34 Dana: what about Anthropic's output stabilization settings? they have a "safety" wrapper and different default temps.
01:03:45 Arjun: with Anthropic mapping, Anthropic's "max_tokens_to_sample" => Redwood "max_tokens", and "temperature" is direct. For safety you can enable Redwood's response filters or hook a safety function. Also we support prompt templates and guardrails via the Console's pre-processing step.

01:04:22 Maya: Together customers often use the streaming WebSocket approach and the Together SDK. Redwood supports streaming over chunked HTTP and WebSocket with the same partial token semantics — we'll show an example.
01:04:40 Arjun: showing streaming example, we stream delta tokens with top-level metadata; function calls are supported: Redwood's "tools" field maps to Together's tooling and OpenAI's function calling. In practice, switching is a header + payload mapping and one small change in post-processing for the tool result shape if you rely on exact proto.

01:05:12 Oliver (Product): any gotchas around embeddings? we use embeddings from OpenAI for semantic search.
01:05:20 Arjun: yes embeddings are supported; we have a dedicated embeddings endpoint and vector size differences depend on model. We provide a migration notebook to compare similarity and retrain the ANN index if necessary.

01:06:05 Priya: security, again — data retention, delete-on-demand, customer-data isolation for logs? we cannot have tokens stored retention > 30d without approval.
01:06:18 Sofia: by default hosted API has short retention and you can opt out; Dedicated and Private have customer-controlled retention. We offer KMS integration and support for bringing your own keys for Private. Audit logs and SAML/SSO are standard for enterprise.

01:07:03 Liam: benchmark question — we need per-token cost targets and p95 latency under load. How do we measure across redwood flavors?
01:07:15 Arjun: two paths: quick hosted sandbox for functional parity, and a Dedicated benchmark run where we spin up a reserved pool and run your workload (same prompts, batching pattern). Optimize suggestions will recommend quantization profile and batching window to hit cost targets. i'll set that up.

01:08:05 Maya: let's walk through a parity example — we took a sample prompt from Fluxlytics. here's the OpenAI call and the Redwood mapped call. watch for stop sequences — OpenAI uses string array "stop"; Anthropic uses hints — we convert both to Redwood's stop param which accepts array or regex.
01:08:28 Liam: nice. what about streaming chunk sizes? we saw some client-side buffering issues.
01:08:36 Arjun: you can configure chunk sizes in SDK and Console, default is optimized for latency. Also prefix/KV cache behavior can change effective token counts on repeat requests — Redwood does automatic prefix caching which reduces cost for many patterns.

01:09:20 Dana: what's required to run a migration POC? we need examples, test harness, cost estimates, security review — timeline target is end of Q2.
01:09:32 Maya: typical POC: 1) parity mapping doc + quickstart; 2) sample benchmark run in Dedicated sandbox (1–2 weeks); 3) security review + contract; 4) pilot with production keys. We can accelerate some steps.

01:10:01 Priya: can we get the SOC 2 and architecture diagram today?
01:10:05 Sofia: i'll email the security pack after the call, it includes SOC 2, diagrams, KMS notes, and a runbook for private deployment.

01:11:12 Arjun: quick demo of Console Optimize — it surfaces suggestions: batching window, model quantization level (e.g., int8 vs fp16), and recommended routing to cheaper model variant for non-critical requests. shows expected cost savings and estimated latency change.
01:11:40 Liam: about model variants — do you automatically fallback to a compatible variant if a region is saturated?
01:11:48 Arjun: yes, smart routing policy can fallback between hosted variants or route to Dedicated if configured; we surfaced a live example in Console where a canary is running.

01:12:30 Maya: pricing — we'll send more detailed pricing but high level: hosted per-token pricing, Dedicated reserved capacity and overage, and Private licensing. For benchmarking we'll include expected cost ranges for the sample workload.

01:13:05 Dana: any limitations for function calling? we do nested calls sometimes and rely on exact JSON ordering.
01:13:16 Arjun: function calling is supported; minor differences in ordering may appear due to tokenization but payload semantics remain the same. We'll produce a mapping page for function outputs and tests to validate.

01:14:05 Oliver: what's the simplest test we can run this week?
01:14:12 Maya: we'll send a parity script: change header, swap model name, run with your sample corpus, and compare outputs and token counts. Should take a couple hours for basic sampling.

01:15:00 Dana: ok let's talk logistics — procurement docs?
01:15:06 Maya: procurement and contract templates are available; sales will send terms. Also, we have a dedicated onboarding engineer for Dedicated/Private deployments.

01:16:22 Priya: small nit — audit logs retention for Hosted vs Dedicated?
01:16:28 Sofia: Hosted: limited retention by default but options exist; Dedicated: you control log retention and can export to your SIEM. Private: full on-prem logs.

01:17:05 Liam: do you have a migration checklist? tokenization, stop sequence mapping, function calls, streaming, embeddings, retraining vector index, security signoffs, benchmark results.
01:17:18 Maya: yes — we'll send the checklist as part of the parity mapping doc.

01:18:45 Arjun: technical deep dive highlight — kv/prefix cache: repeated prompts can see per-token savings; for stateful chat we keep kv cache pinned and can shard across GPUs. For latency-sensitive small requests we recommend smaller batching windows and a higher priority routing.

01:20:01 Dana: any known incompatibilities with Together's SDK? we currently rely on Together-specific session semantics.
01:20:12 Arjun: generally straightforward. Together's session features map to Redwood session tokens; we documented edge cases where last-token flush semantics differ. We'll include a compatibility table.

01:21:30 Maya: recap of next steps — i'm going to send parity doc and quickstart, Sofia sends security pack, Arjun provisions benchmark cluster, and Dana will share corpus and success criteria.

01:22:05 Dana: sounds good, we'll aim to get the corpus to you by Tuesday. end-of-Q2 target still on.

01:22:15 Liam: quick follow-up — is there a sample cost-sensitivity analysis we can see? e.g., what happens if we switch 30% of calls to a cheaper variant.
01:22:28 Arjun: yes Optimize produces that; we'll include a sample spreadsheet.

01:23:00 Maya: any other questions?
01:23:05 Priya: nothing else, thanks.
01:23:10 Oliver: all good.

01:23:30 Maya: thanks everyone — will follow up with artifacts. meeting adjourned.
